facts: Authentication and payment processing will be external.
Accounts will be a standalone service with its own repository.
The Accounts production domain and deployment repository identity are mary.is.
The mary.is Laravel Cloud environment builds with PHP 8.5 and Node 24, including Composer install, npm ci, and the Vite production build.
Logres is the first product consumer.
Products will not share direct database credentials with Accounts.
Accounts is the public source of truth for approved legal and compliance documents.
Applications integrate through a reusable Accounts client package.
Stripe is the selected external payment provider.
The official Stripe PHP SDK is installed behind the Accounts Stripe adapter.
Signed Stripe subscription events idempotently update Accounts entitlements.
Accounts is the public business and product website submitted for Stripe review.
Every configured product feeds the shared pricing, billing, and Stripe-readiness surfaces.
Every documented product receives a public behavior reference generated from the central product registry.
Accounts publishes product families for Accounts Client, Aleph, Bindle, Burdgeon, Funes, Kilgore, Logres, and Menard.
Burdgeon expands to Business Understanding and Relationship Diagram Generation Engine for Organizational Navigation.
Every current product family has an in-development Free tier and Paid tier with separate capability lists.
Free tiers do not require Stripe Price IDs; every Paid tier blocks Stripe readiness until its price and Stripe Price ID are configured.
Accounts consumes the tagged Official Burd Design package from https://github.com/sifrious/official-burd-design for its public interface.
assumptions: One external identity provider can support browser and future NativePHP clients.
The first entitlement required for launch is logres.access.
A relational database is sufficient for account and entitlement state.

decisions.decision: Use a central account service rather than a shared user database.
decisions.rationale: Products need one stable identity without shared-schema ownership.

decisions.decision: Use a separate Accounts client package for login integration and authenticated service calls.
decisions.rationale: Connected applications need one provider-independent integration without duplicated security-sensitive behavior.

decisions.decision: Use Stripe as the external payment provider behind an Accounts adapter.
decisions.rationale: Stripe is the selected provider; keeping it behind Accounts prevents provider objects and webhook policy from leaking into products.

decisions.decision: Use the configuration-backed product registry as the public pricing and billing catalog for the first product.
decisions.rationale: One real product does not justify persisted plan administration; revisit when a second product needs runtime price management.

open_questions: Which external identity provider will be used for the first production login?
Which identity protocol and token audience will Logres consume?
What is the production domain for Logres?
Which Stripe products and prices map to the initial Logres entitlements?
Which legal and compliance documents are approved for initial publication?
What business name, support contacts, business address, and Logres price should be published?
What outage grace period may Logres use for a previously observed entitlement?
constraints: No passwords, MFA secrets, raw payment instruments, or product-domain records in Accounts.
Provider-specific identity and payment types do not cross public service contracts.
Every state-changing provider callback is authenticated and idempotent.
The first deployment targets Laravel Cloud.
